bullets.title: Tech/Semi selloff: OpenAI IPO delay + memory cost inflation drive Asia rout into US open
bullets.body: Nasdaq futures down ~120bps, S&P down ~50bps as Asian markets fell 2-6% overnight. Catalysts: OpenAI leaning toward delaying IPO to 2027 (unable to achieve $1T valuation), Trump admin requesting staggered GPT-5.6 release for security review, and AAPL/MSFT price hikes (15-25% on Mac/iPad, third Xbox hike in 13 months) flagging memory cost inflation. KOSPI dropped ~6% on Samsung investment announcement spooking semi supply dynamics.

bullets.title: Citi cuts IT/Semis/Hardware to Market Weight; Mag 7 down 7% YTD with limited bottom-fishing appetite
bullets.body: Citi US Equity Strategy downgraded Information Technology, Semis, and Hardware from Overweight to Market Weight, citing four Mag 7 headwinds: funding concerns, company-specific issues (AAPL margins, MSFT Azure upside limits, AMZN consumer exposure, GOOGL capex, AVGO/NVDA competition), and technicals breaking 200DMA. Software & Services upgraded to Market Weight.

bullets.title: Memory shortage structural through 2028: MU beat drives read-across, but Samsung/SK Hynix capex spooks supply
bullets.body: Micron reported $41.5B fiscal 3Q revenue at 81% operating margin, signed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements with $100B+ minimum revenue and price floors above prior cycle peaks, and guided memory tightness through 2027. Samsung planning ₩1,000 trillion (~$648B) 10-year capex in chips/AI/displays (announcement June 29); SK Hynix also preparing major investment reveal. MLCC spot prices up 15-20%, AI server-grade parts up 50-60%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor pre-market broadly -3 to -5%; software/enterprise names modestly positive
bullets.body: MU, SNDK, AAOI all -5.1% pre-market; WDC -4.4%; MRVL -3.9%; LITE -3.8%; AMD -3.3%; INTC -3.0%. Offsetting moves in software: NOW +1.5%, PLTR +1.7%, MSFT +1.3%, ADBE +1.2%, TEAM +1.2%. Rotation from semiconductor momentum into defensive software accelerating.

bullets.title: Big Tech as funding source: Goldman/BofA see rotation from Mag 7 into semis and memory
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs views Big Tech selling as the funding source for rotation into semis and memory stocks. BofA flags liquidity flowing from megacap AI arms racers into semiconductors and illiquid cyclicals ahead of a Trump affordability pivot. Market seen as underweighting capex-heavy 'buyers of shortage' vs near-term EPS drivers ('sellers of shortage').

bullets.title: JPM raises S&P 500 YE target to 7,800; maintains tactically bullish but flags momentum crowding risk
bullets.body: Dubravko raises YE26 SPX PT from 7,600 to 7,800 driven by ~10% FY26/FY27 EPS upgrades; 2026 EPS estimate at $350 (+29% y/y), 2027 at $390 (+15%). US GDP growth expected to settle at 1.5-1.75% in H2 after ~3% 2Q. Fed on hold through 2026; unemployment forecast 4.1% in 4Q26. Momentum positioning at sustained highs with elevated flash-crash risk in Low Quality and Speculative Growth. JPM recommends NDX>SPX calls, sell GOOGL/MSFT puts.

bullets.title: Quarter/month-end rebalancing adds selling pressure: Goldman $30B, JPM $165B in estimated equity supply
bullets.body: Goldman estimates $30B of US equities selling into month/quarter-end (89th percentile); JPMorgan estimates ~$165B equity selling paired with bond buying. Mechanical flows compounding the fundamental tech weakness heading into Friday close.

bullets.title: Fed Williams 'well positioned'; Warsh bolsters inflation credibility; Morgan Stanley sees hold through 2026
bullets.body: NY Fed's Williams says current monetary policy stance 'well positioned' for 2% inflation target, expecting moderation in coming quarters. Fed Chair Warsh's debut bolsters inflation credibility; 10-year breakevens dropped ~30bp to ~2.2% since mid-May. Morgan Stanley more comfortable with Fed on hold through 2026 if core PCE stays ≤0.2% m/m; rate hike risk if unemployment falls below 4.0% or inflation runs ≥0.3% m/m. JPM separately flags potential 50-100bp mid-cycle tightening risk, with 10Y Treasuries potentially rising 50bp.

bullets.title: European quant strategy rotates to 'Contraction' phase; overweight Quality/Value, underweight Growth
bullets.body: JPMorgan's European QMI shifted to 'Contraction' after two years in 'Recovery,' with 5 of 6 inputs falling. High Risk has outperformed High Quality by +50% since May 2024 trough, but mean-reversion risk rising. Recommended overweights: Health Care, Energy, Staples, Utilities; underweights: Real Estate, Communication Services, Industrials, Discretionary. US top 10 stocks also at near long-run extreme Growth vs. Value exposure.

bullets.title: Consumer spending data remains healthy despite tariff/macro noise; retail stocks at 25th percentile NTM PE
bullets.body: 22V Research maintains long retail stance citing real personal spending growth ~2%, nominal ~5%, income growth 4-4.5%. PNC/BAC show lower-income consumers increasing spend; Johnson Redbook same-store sales accelerated to 10% YoY; Fiserv dollar volume growth +7.16% YoY; OpenTable dining at 99.7th percentile. Visa spending momentum index broadening. Retail stocks trade at 25th percentile NTM PE spread vs S&P 1500.

bullets.title: AAPL price hikes 15-25% on Mac/iPad: memory cost pass-through signals inventory depletion, potential EPS upside
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac, iPad, and Home product prices 15-25% (absolute $30-$500) driven by DRAM/NAND cost pressures following Micron's memory shortage guidance through 2028. Magnitude earlier and larger than expected (MS had modeled 5-10%); JPM noted mid-single-digit iPhone increase expectations were too optimistic. No iPhone hikes yet; potential increases with September iPhone 18 launch. JPM specialist view: memory cost anxiety overpriced as hikes offset input costs, supporting record margins.

bullets.title: CIO survey: AI/security budgets surging, enterprise apps budgets declining; 62% have AI in meaningful production
bullets.body: IT budget growth for 2026 at 3.9%, 2027 at 4.0%, above prior expectations driven by AI and security. Security budget growth jumped 130bps to 4.4%; 84% of CIOs expect to meet or exceed AI token/credit budgets. Enterprise applications seeing net priority declines: MSFT, NOW, ORCL, CRM, ADBE all down; only Workday and SAP up. 62% of respondents have AI in meaningful production, up 20 points vs. 2H25. Claude implementation overtook ChatGPT but trails Copilot.

bullets.title: WTI crude -3.3% to ~$69-70; Saudi OSP cuts signal supply overhang
bullets.body: WTI down 3.3-3.5% to ~$69-70 on rising Middle Eastern supplies; Brent down ~3.1%. Saudi Arabia likely cutting OSPs for crude to Asia by $6.50-$8.00/barrel in August. EU extends tariff suspension on US products in Boeing-Airbus dispute. Oil pressure compounds broader risk-off, though Hormuz remains open.

bullets.title: Samsung $648B 10-year capex blueprint: positive read-through for semiconductor equipment makers
bullets.body: Samsung planning ₩1,000 trillion (~$648B) investment over 10 years spanning chips, AI data centers, batteries, and displays; formal announcement expected June 29 at presidential office. Applied Materials notes DRAM WFE spend expected to be 2x NAND spend. Citi views the mega-capex plan as a positive for semiconductor equipment makers broadly; ASML EUV capacity guide of 90 tools seen as floor with potential upside to 110-120 if customers commit.

bullets.title: Data center buildout shifting from engineering to political-economy problem; Virginia $0.011/kWh tax largely passable
bullets.body: JPM flags data center social license risks as underpriced by the market; power availability increasingly a strategic constraint for AI infrastructure deployment. Virginia approved $0.011/kWh tax on data center electricity consumption, impact expected manageable and largely passed to customers. Taiwan raised 2026-35 power demand growth forecast to 2.5% CAGR from 1.7%, driven by AI data centers (3-4GW by 2035) and semiconductor fabs.

bullets.title: AI advertising deployment accelerating post-Cannes; AMZN ad business a key AI beneficiary at 46% margins
bullets.body: Cannes Lions marked a shift from AI hesitation to active agency deployment with agentic AI. JPM projects AMZN advertising at ~$83B in 2026 (+21% FXN YoY) at ~46% operating margins (~$38B OI), with AI/ML improving ad ranking and ROAS. AI agents seen expanding digital ad TAM rather than cannibalizing; retail media benefits from improved personalization. Prime Video estimated at $7-8B annualized ad revenue (~8-10% of total). OpenAI ad threat viewed as limited at $2.5B 2026 revenue.

bullets.title: Hong Kong/China tech at 52-week lows; BABA -20% YTD, Asian semi equipment stocks +150-500% YTD divergence
bullets.body: 379 of 410 Asian stocks at 52-week lows; major Chinese tech under pressure (Tencent -18% YTD, Alibaba -19%, BYD -42%, Xiaomi -62%). Stark divergence: Chinese semiconductor equipment stocks surging (GigaDevice +507% YTD, AMEC +248%, NAURA +148%). Korea/Taiwan seeing ETF outflows of $6.2B and $4.0B respectively in the latest week.

bullets.title: ECB inflation expectations moderating but JPM still expects September hike; eurozone/German recovery slow
bullets.body: ECB Consumer Expectations Survey: median 1-year inflation fell 0.5pp to 3.5% in May; 3- and 5-year expectations steady at 2.9% and 2.4%. JPM expects another ECB rate hike in September despite moderation as expectations remain 1pp above pre-conflict levels. German GDP growth expected to accelerate to 1.4% YoY by 2027; composite PMI declined 0.8pt to stagnant levels in June with Special Infrastructure Fund only 34% deployed.

bullets.title: SpaceX Starlink mobile US consumer launch in planning; T, VZ, TMUS largely unfazed in pre-market
bullets.body: SpaceX planning to launch a new Starlink mobile service for US consumers. T, VZ, and TMUS were largely unchanged in pre-market following the news, suggesting market is not yet pricing in material competitive disruption.

bullets.title: MSFT faces Italian antitrust probe over Microsoft 365/Copilot price hike disclosure practices
bullets.body: Italy's AGCM launched an investigation into Microsoft Ireland Operations and Microsoft S.r.l. for allegedly failing to clearly disclose that Microsoft 365 was integrated with Copilot/Designer AI services, and for defaulting consumers onto higher-priced plans. Conduct seen as potentially violating consumer protection rules; adds to regulatory headline risk alongside existing memory cost and margin pressures.
